2ad09e18-9732-5d7a-9af3-e3abf270533f.questionEn: Fill in the past of sein for ich: I was sick yesterday.
2ad09e18-9732-5d7a-9af3-e3abf270533f.explanationDe: Bei sein sagt man meistens war: Ich war gestern krank.
2ad09e18-9732-5d7a-9af3-e3abf270533f.explanationEn: With sein, German mostly uses **war** (was): Ich war gestern krank.
2ad09e18-9732-5d7a-9af3-e3abf270533f.reason: DaF review #4 (A1.2) MAJOR 5: „Für sein benutzt man war, nicht das Perfekt.“ is false as a rule of German (ist gewesen exists); the course practises the common form. Round 11: the cue check now reads every servable item (DaF review #10 found an English cue on a sibling the served-only check had missed); „Präteritum“ in the cue is a term the course never teaches — „gestern“ and the one-word gap already ask for war.

fbdca573-c715-59fb-bc45-d93d44186dd5.explanationDe: Preise sagt man meistens so: zuerst Euro, dann Cent: vier Euro zwanzig. Auch richtig: vier Euro und zwanzig Cent, oder kurz: vier zwanzig.
fbdca573-c715-59fb-bc45-d93d44186dd5.explanationEn: Prices are usually said euros first, then cents: vier Euro zwanzig. Also correct: vier Euro und zwanzig Cent, or short: vier zwanzig.
fbdca573-c715-59fb-bc45-d93d44186dd5.reason: Round 11: the item became servable once A1.2 stopped counting accepted alternatives as lexis (DaF review #10, B1). Its explanation called „und" wrong and the answer set refused the common forms; both are correct German.
